headline: Stocks sit near records even as oil and yields climb
body: Major indices head into the week within sight of records: the S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,811.54, up 0.6% and just shy of its all-time high, while the Dow added 0.8% to 51,654.95 and the Nasdaq rose 0.6% to 27,366.17. Monday's session is thin -- US cash Treasuries are closed for Columbus Day and futures are only modestly higher -- so the tape is being driven more by backdrop than fresh flow. That backdrop is uneasy: a wave of tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, including a strike off Qatar last week, has pushed Brent crude back above $100 and prompted the US to add a third carrier group to the region. The 10-year Treasury yield sits near 5.24%, close to a 24-year high, a combination that would normally pressure equities but hasn't broken the uptrend yet.

The week's real test starts Tuesday, when JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo report, followed by Morgan Stanley and Bank of America on Wednesday -- a sector that has lagged the broader market, with bank stocks down roughly 7.5% over the past month even as the index notches new highs. Wednesday's September CPI print, expected near 3.6% year-over-year, is the week's main catalyst, landing ahead of the Fed's late-October meeting after last month's surprise hike, the central bank's first since 2023. Retail and social chatter offered little fresh signal in today's search -- most of what surfaces on sentiment trackers is residual rather than current -- so this read leans on price action, oil, and rates rather than crowd positioning. Net effect: a market priced for calm sitting on top of several live sources of friction.
